summary:
Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses Part 65 of Zadul-Ma'ad, focusing on how Muslims today have distorted scales in perceiving value and truth. He emphasizes that the light of faith and reliance upon Allah is the greatest gift, incomparable to any material wealth. The lecture addresses how Islam, like all religions, is inherently divisive—separating truth from falsehood—and that this division is natural and necessary, not something to be regretted. He contrasts the early Muslims who were few but steadfast with modern times where material success and celebrity status have replaced scholarly knowledge as markers of authority.

Sh. Mashhour warns against dangerous innovations attacking core Islamic beliefs, including attacks on Sahih Al-Bukhari, the Sunnah, and fundamental doctrines about Allah's attributes and direct interaction with His servants. He criticizes how Muslims have adopted secular, materialistic scales of value from non-Muslim societies, elevating wealthy influencers while marginalizing true scholars. The speaker draws attention to the persecution of Islamic scholars in countries like Bangladesh and Egypt, highlighting how the Ummah has lost its spiritual compass and prioritizes wealth and fame over knowledge and piety.
